head: pr17399-r3
report:
I found one defect that must be fixed before merge, and a probe reproduced it. Remote compaction on Bedrock Mantle checks `/pause` too early, so the compaction request can go out while the session is paused. I didn't measure anything else in the 20 minutes.

## Compaction on Bedrock Mantle is sent while paused (SigV4 credentials)

**Mechanism.** The pause check passes before the request is signed. Signing then waits on an AWS credential lookup, and nothing checks the pause again before the request is sent.

- **First check:** `packages/agent/src/compaction/openai.ts:1003` (V1, `requestOpenAiRemoteCompaction`) and `packages/agent/src/compaction/compaction-v2-streaming.ts:325` (V2, once per attempt) both call `holdBeforeDispatch(opts.beforeDispatch, signal)`. The gate is open, so the call returns at once.
- **Actual send:** the next line calls `fetchImpl`. For a Bedrock OpenAI-route model, `fetchImpl` comes from `prepareBedrockCompactionRequest` (`packages/agent/src/compaction/bedrock.ts:36-46`). That function builds `transportFetch(resolvedModel, fetch)` with no hold, then hands it to bedrock-mantle's `prepareRequest`. That returns `createSignedFetch` (`packages/ai/src/providers/bedrock-mantle.ts:29-59`), which runs three awaits before sending:
  1. `await requestBody(...)`
  2. `await resolveAwsCredentials(...)`, which may contact a container or IMDS endpoint, run a `credential_process`, or call SSO or STS. It uses `withoutDispatchHold(baseFetch)`.
  3. `await signRequest(...)`

  Then it calls `baseFetch(...)`, and `baseFetch` has no hold at all.
- **What changes in between:** a human runs `/pause` during the credential lookup or signing. Nothing checks the gate again, so the paid compaction request is sent anyway.
- **The comment is wrong:** the comment at `openai.ts:999-1002` says "the attestation, metadata and Bedrock signing above all await". Signing doesn't happen above the hold; it happens inside `fetchImpl`, after it.

**Scope.** Normal Mantle turns don't have this problem: they go through `withTransportFetch(model, options)`, so the signed fetch's `baseFetch` keeps the hold and checks it again after signing. Only the compaction path builds its transport without the hold. In production, `session-maintenance.ts:3724` and `:5639` pass `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(signal)` as `beforeDispatch`, so manual and automatic compaction are both affected.

**Trigger.**
- Model: provider `bedrock-mantle`, baseUrl `https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/openai/v1`, no bearer token, so SigV4 is used.
- Call `requestOpenAiRemoteCompaction` or `requestCompactionV2Streaming` with `beforeDispatch: agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(signal)`.
- Engage `agentPauseGate.pause()` while AWS credentials are being resolved. The probe does this with `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI`, and the fetch mock engages the pause when it serves the credentials.

**Command and output:**
```
cd /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/heads/670df28f7bf7/packages/agent && \
  bun test /mnt/nvme/tmp-omp-batch/reviewer-gap-rederive/a/rederive/scratch/rederive__pr17399-r3__t4/mantle-pause.test.ts
```
```
V1: completed 
  creds lookup; pause engaged -> paused=true
  POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-west-2.api.aws/openai/v1/responses/compact sent while paused=true
(fail) V1 remote compaction on Bedrock Mantle (SigV4): pause engaged during credential lookup [179.81ms]
V2: completed 
  creds lookup; pause engaged -> paused=true
  POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-west-2.api.aws/openai/v1/responses sent while paused=true
(fail) V2 streaming compaction on Bedrock Mantle (SigV4): pause engaged during credential lookup [11.54ms]

 0 pass
 2 fail
```
In both paths the compaction finished during the pause instead of waiting for the resume.

**Fix direction.** Pass the hold through `prepareBedrockCompactionRequest` into `transportFetch(resolvedModel, fetch, beforeDispatch)`, so the gate is checked again after signing, at the actual send. That is how the normal stream path already works. Then correct the comment at `openai.ts:999-1002`. A second `holdBeforeDispatch` before `fetchImpl` would not fix it, because it would still run before the credential and signing awaits.
